rankingModel.rationale: Michelin and James Beard judge food specifically; crowd ratings measure whole-experience satisfaction and are better at detecting badness than greatness. Thin review samples are shrunk toward the prior.
rankingModel.slateRule: Order by food-first score, but compose the five so both kinds of evidence are represented. Expert- and critic-backed picks lead. At least one slot is reserved for the strongest crowd-verified local favorite (highest adjusted rating with a meaningful review base) even when an expert-backed candidate would otherwise take it. A beloved neighborhood spot with no Michelin attention still belongs on the list; it just doesn't lead it.

high_end_dc.name: Albi

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Washingtonian's reigning #1 restaurant; Resy tables for the hearth-side seats go within minutes of release.

high_end_dc.why: Michael Rafidi's live-fire Palestinian tasting menu is the most emotionally resonant fine dining in the city — Michelin star, James Beard win, and Washingtonian's top spot two years running.

high_end_dc.name: Omakase at Barracks Row

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Small counter, Michelin star and Washingtonian #4 — book 4–6 weeks ahead.

high_end_dc.reservationNote: Book on Resy; Tue–Sat 5:30–11 PM, closed Sun–Mon. Phone (202) 481-1640.
high_end_dc.why: Nakazawa-trained Ricky Wang's counter moves from sweet shrimp in smoked uni sauce to hay-smoked mackerel nigiri with exacting rice and fish — the city's most thrilling omakase at its price.

high_end_dc.name: Jônt

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Single nightly seating at a tiny counter above Maketto; books out weeks ahead.

high_end_dc.why: A blink-and-you'll-miss-it counter earning two Michelin stars for technically dazzling French-meets-Japanese courses in a room that seats barely a dozen.

high_end_dc.name: Fiola

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Prime weekend tables need 2-3 weeks' notice; walk-ins rarely land a seat.

high_end_dc.why: Fabio Trabocchi's marble-and-crystal dining room delivers hand-rolled-pasta grandeur with a nearly thousand-review track record of consistency.

high_end_dc.name: Minibar by José Andrés

reservationDifficulty.label: Very Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Only ~14 seats; reservations release online at an exact time each quarter and vanish within seconds.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: L'Auberge Chez François

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Reservations release roughly 60 days out; prime weekend slots for the eight-course menu vanish fast.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Phone/walk-in only — call ahead, no online booking.
high_end_mclean_tysons.why: A century-old Alsatian institution in a Great Falls farmhouse that still out-romances every newer tasting menu in the region.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Ingle Korean Steakhouse

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: NoVA Magazine's #3 restaurant for 2026 and a Washingtonian 100 regular; prime weekend dinner slots go well in advance, though walk-ins are accepted.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Not bookable on OpenTable; reserve via inglekoreansteakhouse.com or call (202) 845-4966 (number on its OpenTable listing). Walk-ins accepted.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Nostos

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Bookable a few weeks out on OpenTable; Friday/Saturday prime times go first.

high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Tableside saganaki flames and whole grilled fish turn a Tysons office-park address into the DMV's most convincing Athens stand-in.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Modan

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: The omakase counter seats only 8–10 at 5:30 and 8:30 and needs a $50 deposit, so book about a week ahead; à la carte tables are easier.

high_end_mclean_tysons.reservationNote: Book online (OpenTable). Omakase is $170 or $260 per person with a $50 deposit, forfeited if you cancel within 24 hours.

high_end_mclean_tysons.name: Wren

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: OpenTable shows broad same-week availability; weekend prime time fills a few days out.

high_end_mclean_tysons.why: Chef Yo Matsuzaki runs an izakaya with real backbone, from rich ramen to robata-style small plates and an 18–20-course omakase, 14 floors above Tysons.

high_end_reston.name: Heirloom

high_end_reston.why: A hidden speakeasy upstairs from Open Road where chef Dane Sewlall's wagyu meatballs and short-rib plates are cooked with far more care than the clubby setting suggests.

high_end_reston.name: Clarity (Reston)

reservationDifficulty.note: New 175-seat room; weekends fill a few days out, weeknights generally open.

high_end_reston.name: The Simon at Reston Station

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Hotel dining room; OpenTable shows same-day and next-day slots most nights.

high_end_reston.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable; Schar Bar for walk-ins.
high_end_reston.why: Tableside duck à la presse and a roaming cheese cart make this the most theatrical, special-occasion cooking in Reston, rooted in Mid-Atlantic ingredients.

high_end_reston.name: Davio's Northern Italian Steakhouse (Reston)

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Big room at the Wiehle-Reston Metro; weeknights are walk-in friendly, weekends book a few days out.

high_end_reston.reservationNote: Book on davios.com or call (888) 995-4810; it no longer takes OpenTable bookings.

high_end_reston.chainRationale: Ghazal's pick: she vouches for the Reston Station location.

high_end_nova.name: Nasime

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard

high_end_nova.name: Elyse

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Only 30 seats and a single nightly tasting seating; reserve well in advance.

high_end_nova.name: Le Refuge

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Small, snug dining room; call ahead for weekend evenings.

high_end_nova.reservationNote: Phone/walk-in only — call ahead, no online booking.
high_end_nova.why: Unapologetically old-school bouillabaisse-and-duck-a-l'orange cooking that has outlasted every trend in Old Town for three decades.

high_end_nova.name: Clarity

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Tasting-menu seatings are limited nightly; book 2-3 weeks ahead for weekends.

high_end_nova.why: A kitchen that treats a Vienna strip-mall storefront as a stage for genuine special-occasion cooking, plated like still-lifes.

high_end_nova.name: Harrimans Grill

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: OpenTable advises booking 2–3 weeks ahead; ~20 bookings/day; dinner Wed–Sun only.

high_end_nova.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable 2–3 weeks out for weekend dinner; dinner Wed–Sun 5–9:30 PM.
high_end_nova.why: Hunt-country sourcing meets serious grill technique — wood-fired local beef and Chesapeake seafood plated with resort-level polish, making it the most complete destination dinner in Loudoun.

moderate_dc.name: Daru

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Weekend Resy slots vanish fast on James Beard buzz; weeknights and the bar are easier.

moderate_dc.why: Turns Indian comfort food into a genuinely exciting tasting menu at a price that still lets you order a second round of naan without flinching.

moderate_dc.name: Tapori

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy books out on weekends but midweek tables and walk-in bar seats are attainable.

moderate_dc.why: South Asian street food as serious craft — chaat and kathi rolls sharp enough to make you forget you're paying moderate-tier prices.

reservationDifficulty.label: Hard
reservationDifficulty.note: Small wine-bar footprint means Resy tables disappear almost instantly; expect a wait or an early walk-in.

moderate_dc.name: Anju

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy tables open weekly and go quickly for weekend prime time, but bar/counter walk-in seats are usually available.

moderate_dc.why: Soulful, funky-fermented Korean plates and the city's best banchan spread make this the rare date-night spot that never feels like it's trying too hard.

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Resy recommended for weekend dinner; walk-in seats at the bar or patio often available.

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

moderate_reston.reservationNote: Book through the website or Google, or call.

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

moderate_nova.name: Osteria Marzano

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

moderate_nova.reservationNote: Book on OpenTable a few days ahead for weekends.

moderate_nova.name: Evelyn Rose

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

moderate_nova.why: A cozy, ingredient-forward newcomer to Church Street that plays it fresh and unfussy — exactly the low-key-special dinner Vienna needed.

moderate_nova.name: Chef Tan

reservationDifficulty.note: Waitlist-driven since the WaPo 3-star review; arrive at opening or expect a wait at weekend dinner.

casual_dc.name: Dog Tag Bakery

casual_dc.name: Baked and Wired

casual_dc.why: Georgetown's best cup of coffee comes with a cupcake that actually earns the hype, at prices that predate the neighborhood's gentrification.

casual_dc.name: El Rinconcito Cafe

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Zamarod Afghan Cuisine

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Autentico

casual_mclean_tysons.why: Sharp, lime-bright ceviche carretillero and a smoky wok-tossed lomo saltado bring real Lima flavor to a Great Falls strip center.

casual_mclean_tysons.name: Amoo's Restaurant

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate

casual_mclean_tysons.why: The chelo kabob McLean regulars measure every other Persian grill against — simple, classic, and consistently right.

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy

casual_reston.why: Fresh, lemony Mediterranean plates and wraps that have quietly been feeding South Lakes for years.

casual_reston.name: Pollo Peru

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Counter service.

casual_reston.why: Charcoal-blistered pollo a la brasa with the requisite green sauce — the NoVA staple done well.

casual_reston.name: Lake Anne Coffee House & Wine Bar

reservationDifficulty.label: Easy
reservationDifficulty.note: Walk-in; patio seats go fast on market Saturdays.

casual_nova.name: Maharani Palace

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: Reservations recommended for dinner and weekends; bar seating available for walk-ins.

casual_nova.why: A Herndon storefront with white-tablecloth ambition at strip-mall prices — the tandoor (and nearly 4,000 five-star-leaning reviews) don't lie.

casual_nova.name: Stracci Pizza

reservationDifficulty.label: Moderate
reservationDifficulty.note: No reservations; weekend-night waits are common at this small neighborhood spot.

casual_nova.why: A Del Ray storefront turning out blistered, hand-pulled pies with obsessive dough work that usually costs twice as much elsewhere.

casual_nova.name: Taco Bamba

happy_hour_dc.name: Your Only Friend

happy_hour_mclean_tysons.name: Joon

reservationDifficulty.note: Weeknights are easy, but the Sunday jazz brunch fills quickly and needs booking several days ahead.
